incident-bot: PagerDuty -> incident fired: PD#12345 - DB high connections on redwood-prod-primary (pg-main). alert: pg_max_connections 95% (currently 950/1000), errors=502 from web tier, read latency p95 1.8s. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345

jess (oncall): acked. I'm taking it. tagging @alex (db) @maya (sre).

alex (db): on it. what's the customer impact? 502s across web frontends? any writes failing or read-only errors?

jess (oncall): customers seeing 502 and some background jobs failing. writes are getting thrown errors "FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections". cache miss rate spiked ~3x, looks like Redis hit maxclients too.

maya (sre): confirm Redis near maxclients as well. metrics: redis maxclients 10k/10k on cache-prod-1, evictions increasing. this likely cascaded -> more DB queries.

nick (platform): PD escalation: escalation policy to db-team on 2nd tier if not acked in 5m. we've got ack. post links to logs: https://logs.redwood.com/goto/abc123

alex (db): short term plan:
- reduce app concurrency to cut new DB connections
- increase pgbouncer pool_size/connections and restart pgbouncer on app nodes
- ALTER SYSTEM set max_connections = 1200; SELECT pg_reload_conf(); (careful if memory)
- scale Redis node to add capacity (redis-ops)

jess (oncall): doing steps now. flipping feature flag to reduce traffic for non-critical routes: `/flags set_cheap_mode on` (internal flag) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jess (oncall): scaling web deployment down concurrency and restarting workers:
```
kubectl set env deploy/web-prod MAX_WORKER_THREADS=8 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/web-prod -n prod
```

alex (db): applying pgbouncer change on poolers (rolling restart):
```
ssh pooler-1
sudo systemctl restart pgbouncer
# increase pool_size in /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini from 1000 to 1500
```

alex (db): running ALTER SYSTEM now:
```
psql -h redwood-prod-primary -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '1200';"
psql -h redwood-prod-primary -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf();"
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: PD#12345 acknowledged by jess (oncall) at 2026-03-14T16:12:34Z

pagerduty-bot: Alert escalated to second tier (db-team) at 2026-03-14T16:15:01Z - alex (db) paging in progress

maya (sre): scaled Redis cluster by adding a node (redis-prod-2). command: `nomad job dispatch redis-cluster scale count=3`

jess (oncall): Redis connections dropped from 10k to 6.5k after scale, cache hit rate recovering. DB connections dropped to ~680 after pgbouncer restart and app throttling.

alex (db): DB error rate down. p95 read latency back to ~120ms. background jobs still have some retries — will monitor. running quick check:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state NOT IN ('idle'); -- 672
SELECT usename, COUNT(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY usename ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5;
```

jess (oncall): PD note: customer impact - Intermittent 502s for ~30 minutes across several services; impacts: web API requests for search and user profile requests. Severity: SEV2. Customers mostly degraded but no widespread data loss.

nick (platform): handoff: I'm taking post-incident action items. tagging @alex @maya. we'll do follow-up runbook updates for connection pooling + autoscale thresholds.

alex (db): immediate followups:
- formalize pgbouncer pool sizing per node and add automated pooler restarts when conn spikes
- revisit default max_connections on prod families
- add alerting that correlates Redis maxclients -> DB connection surge to reduce noisy signals

maya (sre): add runbook note: if both Redis and DB spike, first action: scale Redis, enable app cheap-mode, increase pgbouncer pools, consider failover only if primary is unhealthy.

jess (oncall): handing off to night team in 20m. leaving notes in incident channel and PD. thanks everyone. :heart:

pagerduty-bot: PD#12345 status: resolved by jess (oncall) at 2026-03-14T17:05:02Z

jess (oncall): closing thread here. will file postmortem with timeline + graphs. assigning owners: alex (db) -> DB followups, maya (sre) -> Redis/autoscale, nick (platform) -> runbook + alerts.
